# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Coding standards — MANDATORY

The `doc/` directory contains the authoritative coding standards for this project.
**All code generated or modified in this repository must comply with these standards.**
Read the relevant document before writing any code in the affected layer.

- `doc/architecture.md` — authoritative reference for module structure, layer
  diagram, dependency rules, data flow, and where new code belongs.
- `doc/analysis_code.md` — variable naming rules for all computation modules
  (`src/atmos/core.py` and any future engine files): symbol-based names, unit suffixes,
  conversion constant usage, function signature conventions.
- `doc/ui.md` — TUI code standards for `src/ui.py`, `src/menu.py`, and `main.py`:
  `rich`/`prompt_toolkit` usage, color palette, workflow pattern, panel and
  table conventions, prompt format, error messages.

## Running the application

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python main.py
```

On startup the app prompts to select an atmospheric model CSV from `src/atmos/data/models/`. The main menu then offers atmospheric property lookups, speed conversions, and speed-altitude chart generation. All calculation inputs come from JSON files in `data/inputs/` — the TUI only asks which file to run.

Tests: `python -m pytest`.

## Packaging

`src/atmos/` is the installable `atmos` package (`pyproject.toml`), consumed by the Life website (`/projects/atmos`) pinned to a release tag tarball. Keep it free of TUI imports (`ui`, `menu`, `logger`, `rich`, `prompt_toolkit`) and of pyplot outside the `plot_speed_alt_*` TUI entry points. Use `draw_speed_alt(fig, ...)` for non-interactive rendering and `use_model(path)` for per-call model selection. After a change the website needs, bump `src/atmos/version.py`, tag `v<version>`, and update the pin in the Life repo.

## Architecture

See `doc/architecture.md` for the authoritative layer diagram, module responsibilities, dependency rules, and data flow. Read it before adding or moving code.

## Configuration — `src/atmos/defaults.json`

Edit this file to change chart axis ranges, grid line values, and solver tolerances without touching code. Key sections:

```
chart_defaults   — alt_min/max, per-type x_min/x_max, mach/kcas/keas/ktas grid arrays, n_altitude_points
solver           — intersection binary-search tol/iterations, vcas_super/mach_super step sizes and error %
data_dir         — path to data directory (default ./data)
log_file         — path for AtmosLog.txt (default ./data/outputs/AtmosLog.txt)
```

Physics constants (`GAMMA = 1.4` etc.) are **not** in config — they are thermodynamic facts.

## Input case files — `data/inputs/*.json`

The TUI selects from these files. Two schemas:

**Speed conversion** (`speed_type`: `mach | ktas | kcas | keas`):
```json
{ "cases": [
    { "alt_ft": 35000, "speed_type": "mach", "speed_value": 0.84 }
] }
```

**Atmospheric properties** (`input_type`: `altitude | pressure`):
```json
{ "cases": [
    { "input_type": "altitude", "value_ft": 35000 },
    { "input_type": "pressure", "value_psf": 499.34 }
] }
```

## Atmospheric model CSV

Files in `src/atmos/data/models/` (selected at startup). Two models ship:
- `standard_atmos.csv` — based on Nelson "Flight Stability and Automatic Control"
- `standard_atmos_1976.csv` — US Standard Atmosphere 1976 (generated by `tools/gen_ussa76.py`)

Required columns: `Hgeo_ft`, `H_ft`, `P_lb/ft2`, `pho/pho0`, `pho_slug/ft3`, `T_degR`. Lines starting with `#` are treated as comments.

## Speed envelope JSON — `src/atmos/data/envelopes/*.json`

Passed to speed-altitude chart functions. Key structure:
- `chart` — axis min/max overrides (overrides `src/atmos/defaults.json`)
- `mach_grid`, `kcas_grid`, `keas_grid`, `ktas_grid` — grid line overrides
- `envelope_boundaries` — list of boundaries with `segments` of `{type, value}` where type is `mach|keas|kcas|ktas`. Intersection altitudes are computed automatically via binary search in KEAS space.

The legacy `speed_limits` key is still accepted for backward compatibility.
